newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares seen rising on blue chips interest.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares seen rising on blue chips interest.

text.p: Leading Russian shares headed higher in early trade on Wednesday and traders said client orders could push the market slightly higher by the close.
The Russian Trading System opened at 355.47 after closing on Tuesday at 355.35.

"Prices are firm and we see that activity in blue chips has increased, sparked by client interest, and that is a big difference from Monday to yesterday," said Pavel Gronbjerg, co-head trader at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Utility UES rose to $0.3170 at 0915 GMT after closing at $0.3140. Oil company LUKoil headed individual turnover, rising to $15.330 from $15.09.
Gronbjerg said new fund allocations in the West could be behind the growth, but Menatep Bank chief trader Sergei Kosynkin saw Russian and Western money buying in equal proportion.
"The market has been holding on Russian money, not on Western," said Kosynkin, adding he did not think economic indicators released on Tuesday in the United States had much to do with the turnaround.
Dealers saw the index rising a little on healthy volumes by the end of the day, and said the growth could continue to the end of the week.
